name: OpenReward Sandboxes

modes.label: Pay-as-you-go, per second
modes.note: List: $0.0504/vCPU-h, $0.0162/GiB-h, NVIDIA L4 $1.51/GPU-h, billed by the second. Presets CPU:RAM 0.5:0.5 ... 4:16 (RAM 1-4 GiB per vCPU in 1x/2x/4x steps). 4 vCPU/8 GiB = $0.3312/h. Paid from prepaid organization credits (pricing page, checked 2026-11-08).

evidence.quote: By default all egress - all internet access - is allowed

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go
plans.note: Prepaid credits per organization, topped up at openreward.ai/<org>/billing. When the balance is exhausted, API calls return 402 and usage stops (a hard stop, not overage). There is no public free tier or signup credit; academic credits are on request.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: On-prem, dedicated support, custom SLAs; contact sales.

caveats: Sandboxes are tied to an OpenReward environment workspace. The docs say it is 'not a general sandbox compute solution'. It is built for RL and eval environments.

ORS environments 'work with any sandbox provider'. The environment author can run the sandbox on E2B, Daytona or Modal with their own credentials. The documented pattern still creates the sandbox at session start and terminates it at session end. This card prices OpenReward's own sandbox (concepts/sandboxes.md, sandboxes/modal.md, checked 2026-11-08).
Preset CPU:RAM sizes go up to 4 vCPU / 16 GiB in the docs.
The nvidia-l4 preset's vCPU/RAM and whether CPU/RAM are billed on top of $1.51/GPU-h are undocumented; the engine adds the GPU rate on top of resource rates.
Concurrency limits, max lifetime, minimum billed duration, disk and egress pricing are undocumented (null).

No pause, snapshot or fork API is documented. The sandbox is torn down when its session ends. Cloud-storage buckets mount read-only. Network control is the block_network switch, which turns all outbound traffic on or off; no per-host allowlist is documented.

Browser: no built-in browser or desktop stream. You can add a headless browser such as Chromium to your own public linux/amd64 Docker Hub image. No inbound port or URL is documented to view a desktop.
CPU/RAM rates are numerically identical to E2B's list rates; the backend is not disclosed.
Academic credits are available on request (not modelled).

No SSH or inbound URL is documented. Access is through the SDK: run, upload and download. Disk size and disk price are not published (the pricing page lists CPU, memory and L4 GPU only), so extra disk stays unpriced (checked 2026-11-08).

Machine sizes: concepts/sandboxes lists 0.5:0.5 to 4:16 plus nvidia-l4. The sandboxes/openreward page says 'From 0.1:0.1' to 4:16. The official Python SDK added 8:8, 16:16, 8:16, 8:32 and 16:64 in v0.1.159 (2026-09-24); the docs do not list these sizes yet.
Custom sandbox images must be public on Docker Hub and built for linux/amd64 (no private registries, no arm64).

fleet.verification: Prepaid organization credits; further verification unknown.
fleet.notes: Rendered PAYG/Enterprise pricing establishes prepaid usage and custom/on-prem option, not numeric concurrent-environment quota. No verified default count, GPU allowance, verification checklist or approval time. Hosted environment servers default to concurrency 500 sessions per pod and max-scale 10 pods (owner-configurable via `orwd update-link`); beyond that callers get 429 "Environment at maximum capacity". No per-account sandbox concurrency or creation-rate limit is published.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: which will terminate the sandbox as soon as the session ends.
snapshot_auto.note: Lifecycle is start() -> run/upload/download -> stop() (deletion). No pause, sleep or state save documented; SDK 0.1.160 sandbox client exposes only run, check_run, upload, download, start, stop.

snapshot_on_demand.quote:
Available operations:

* `run()`: Execute command and return output
* `check_run()`: Execute command, raise on error if it returns a non-zero exit code
* `upload()`: Upload files to sandbox
* `download()`: Download files from sandbox
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint/fork API in docs or SDK 0.1.160. Only custom (public Docker Hub) images as templates.

harness_api.quote: This launches Claude Code as a subprocess against the terminal-bench-2-verified environment, running 5 tasks from the test split.
harness_api.note: Close but inverted: first-party Firehorse CLI (pip install firehorse-cli) runs claude-code, codex, gemini, resum, react harnesses on the CALLER's machine and proxies their tools (via MCP / session-scoped 'harness toolsets' claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, OpenClaw, Hermes) into the sandbox; writes trajectory.jsonl. The harness does not run inside the sandbox, and there is no API to start/stream/resume an in-sandbox agent.

egress_allowlist.quote: By default all egress - all internet access - is allowed, but there may be use cases where this is problematic: ... To enable network isolation, set `block_network=True`
egress_allowlist.note: Only an all-or-nothing switch: block_network cuts all outbound traffic (SDK: 'disables outbound network access (Kubernetes egress policies required)'). No per-domain or per-IP allow/deny list is documented (concepts/sandboxes, sandboxes/openreward), so not an egress allowlist; open_internet stays true. The secret proxy's per-secret allowed hosts restrict where secrets are injected, not where traffic may go.

egress_http_rules.note: Only network control is the block_network boolean; no method/path/header rules documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Rather than exposing raw secret values inside your environment or sandbox, OpenReward replaces them with placeholders before they reach your server. The actual values are injected on egress - when outbound HTTP requests leave the environment or sandbox, OpenReward swaps the placeholders back in for allowed destination hosts only.
secret_proxy.note: Session `secrets` dict; well-known keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Tavily, HF, Kaggle, E2B, Modal, Daytona...) have default hosts, arbitrary keys via (value, [hosts]) tuple: 'Custom hosts for a secret without defaults'. HTTP only per docs; no DB/SSH/git coverage documented. Scope is per ORS session (environment + sandbox).

volume_attach.note: Only the environment's own cloud bucket, mounted read-only ('Buckets are always mounted read-only'); no writable block/network volumes. SDK ephemeral disk_request/disk_limit fields are commented out.

volume_shared.quote: Key Concept: The same storage is accessible in both environments and sandboxes.
volume_shared.note: Read-only: `read_only: Literal[True]` 'Buckets are always mounted read-only'. Every sandbox of the environment can mount the same bucket (optionally a subdirectory via only_dir) concurrently.

docker_inside.quote: A sandbox is an isolated container for executing arbitrary code.
docker_inside.note: Not documented. Isolation is a container (shared kernel). The sandbox and docker-images docs document no privileged mode and no Docker-in-Docker path.

nested_virt.quote: A sandbox is an isolated container for executing arbitrary code.
nested_virt.note: Not documented. Container isolation (shared kernel); no /dev/kvm or privileged-mode option is documented.

browser.quote: The image must be publicly accessible on Docker Hub. OpenReward pulls images from public repositories.
browser.how: add a headless browser such as Chromium to your own public linux/amd64 Docker Hub image and drive it with run()
browser.note: No built-in browser, Playwright or CDP feature is documented, and no pre-made image ships one. Custom images are the documented path. No inbound port or URL is documented, so the browser is driven from inside the sandbox.

anti_bot.quote: Pay-as-you-go environments. Simple, transparent pricing. You only pay for the resources you use, billed by the second.
anti_bot.note: Not documented. The product is an RL/eval sandbox and environment host; no browser stealth feature is listed.

captcha_solving.quote: Pay-as-you-go environments. Simple, transparent pricing. You only pay for the resources you use, billed by the second.
captcha_solving.note: Not documented. No CAPTCHA-solving feature is listed; the product is a code sandbox and RL environment host.

egress_ip_type.quote: By default all egress - all internet access - is allowed
egress_ip_type.note: derived: sandboxes are cloud-hosted containers with plain internet egress; no residential/mobile proxy or static-IP offering is documented, so outbound traffic is assumed to use ordinary datacenter IPs.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Time-limited: Sessions expire after inactivity or when the session is deleted.
auto_stop_idle.note: Sandbox lifetime is tied to the environment session (`teardown()` calls `sandbox.stop()`); when the session expires from inactivity the sandbox is torn down with it. Not a dedicated per-sandbox idle timer distinct from session expiry.

live_resize.note: `machine_size` is set once in `SandboxSettings` at creation; no API to change CPU/RAM of a running sandbox is documented.

own_agent_api.quote: This launches Claude Code as a subprocess against the terminal-bench-2-verified environment, running 5 tasks from the test split.
own_agent_api.note: Not documented. The firehorse runner drives third-party coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and others) against sandboxes; no OpenReward-owned agent product is documented.

mcp_server.quote: **Subprocess + MCP agents** (claude-code, codex, gemini) launch the respective CLI as a child process and proxy environment tools via [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io).
mcp_server.note: OpenReward proxies its own sandbox-backed tools into third-party MCP-based coding CLIs; no standalone MCP server product for controlling OpenReward sandboxes (e.g. from Claude Desktop) was found in the docs.

lang_python.note: Official SDK is Python (`openreward` package on PyPI); default pre-made sandbox images (`generalreasoning/python-ds:3.12-tools`, `python:3.11-slim`, etc.) are Python-based.

lang_node.note: Node.js is listed as a common out-of-the-box Docker Hub image option for sandboxes; no first-party Node SDK, but a Node runtime image is offered directly.

public_ipv4.quote: OpenReward Sandboxes are tied to an environment workspace on OpenReward which provisions compute. This means it is not a general sandbox compute solution.
public_ipv4.note: Sandboxes are internal execution containers reached only via the OpenReward API (run/upload/download); no public IPv4 per sandbox is documented.

inbound_https.quote: Available operations: run(), check_run(), upload(), download()
inbound_https.note: No feature to expose an HTTPS URL to a sandbox port is documented. Ports appear only for sidecar containers (example ports=[6379]), not for inbound access.

ingress_rules.quote: OpenReward Sandboxes are tied to an environment workspace on OpenReward which provisions compute.
ingress_rules.note: Not documented. No inbound port or URL is documented, so no ingress rules apply.

guest_firewall.note: derived: isolation is `container` (shared kernel), not a full VM/microVM with root, so in-guest nftables/iptables control is not assumed.

static_egress_ip.quote: By default all egress - all internet access - is allowed, but there may be use cases where this is problematic ... To enable network isolation, set `block_network=True`
static_egress_ip.note: Only a network on/off (block_network) toggle is documented; no fixed/static outbound IP feature is mentioned.

open_source.note: The GeneralReasoning GitHub org publishes open-source client tooling (firehorse harness runner, example environment repos) but the core hosted platform (environment server hosting + OpenReward Sandboxes infrastructure) is closed-source SaaS; no OSI license covers the core product.

persistent_disk.quote: In the context of ORS, a sandbox is usually initialised when a new session is created and torn down when the session ends.
persistent_disk.note: No pause, snapshot or fork API is documented (start/run/check_run/upload/download/stop). Cloud-storage buckets are 'always mounted read-only' (https://docs.openreward.ai/storage/buckets.md), so they do not keep files the sandbox writes. Environments can use E2B, Daytona or Modal instead, but OpenReward's Modal guide uses the same lifecycle: 'when a session ends, we terminate the sandbox' (https://docs.openreward.ai/sandboxes/modal.md).

persist_scope.quote: In the context of ORS, a sandbox is usually initialised when a new session is created and torn down when the session ends.
persist_scope.note: No snapshot or restore API and no writable volume are documented; buckets mount read-only (https://docs.openreward.ai/storage/buckets.md).

snapshot.quote:
Available operations:

* `run()`: Execute command and return output
* `check_run()`: Execute command, raise on error if it returns a non-zero exit code
* `upload()`: Upload files to sandbox
* `download()`: Download files from sandbox
snapshot.note: Full lifecycle documented is create -> start() -> run/upload/download -> stop() (delete). No snapshot/checkpoint API anywhere in the docs or SDK.

pause_resume.quote: To delete an OpenReward Sandbox, we use the `stop` method ... which will terminate the sandbox as soon as the session ends.
pause_resume.note: Only start() and stop() lifecycle calls are documented; stop() terminates (deletes) the sandbox rather than pausing it. No pause/resume method exists.

fork.note: No clone/fork operation in the documented sandbox API (start/run/check_run/upload/download/stop only); the only way to get a 'copy' is starting a new sandbox from the same base image.

fork_running.note: Since no fork capability exists at all (see `fork`), forking a still-running sandbox is a fortiori unsupported.

memory_snapshot_fork.note: No memory-snapshot or checkpoint/restore mechanism is documented anywhere; lifecycle is only start/run/upload/download/stop.

ssh.quote:
Available operations:

* `run()`: Execute command and return output
* `check_run()`
* `upload()`: Upload files to sandbox
* `download()`: Download files from sandbox
ssh.note: No SSH is documented. Access is through the SDK run/upload/download calls proxied by the OpenReward API. The docs index (llms.txt) has no SSH or terminal-access page.

desktop.quote: A sandbox is an isolated container for executing arbitrary code. Sandboxes provide secure, temporary compute resources for running untrusted agent code in an ORS environment.
desktop.note: No built-in desktop or stream is documented. A custom image can include Xvfb, but no inbound port or URL is documented to view or stream a desktop (access is run/upload/download only). The docs show no desktop example.

computer_use.quote: A sandbox is an isolated container for executing arbitrary code.
computer_use.note: No screenshot-and-click computer-use API is documented; the sandbox exposes run(), check_run(), upload() and download().

wake_on_request.quote: await sandbox.start()  # Creates the sandbox ... await sandbox.stop() ... which will terminate the sandbox as soon as the session ends.
wake_on_request.note: Sandboxes are explicitly created with start() and torn down (deleted) with stop(); there is no idle/sleep state and thus nothing to 'wake' on an incoming request.

agent_harnesses.quote: This launches Claude Code as a subprocess against the terminal-bench-2-verified environment, running 5 tasks from the test split.
agent_harnesses.note: Coding-agent harnesses (claude-code, codex, gemini, resum, react) run via the first-party 'firehorse-cli' as a subprocess on the CALLER's own machine (proxying tools into the sandbox over MCP/toolsets), not preinstalled inside the sandbox container. The pre-made sandbox images (docker-images.md) are `generalreasoning/python-ds:3.12-tools` and `generalreasoning/knowledge-worker` — neither ships a coding-agent CLI.

windows.note: Sandbox infra is explicitly Linux/amd64 container-based; no Windows OS option exists anywhere in the docs.

macos.quote: OpenReward's sandbox infrastructure runs on `linux/amd64`. If you're building custom images on an ARM machine (e.g. Apple Silicon), you'll need to target this platform explicitly — more on this below.
macos.note: Sandboxes are Linux/amd64 Docker containers only; macOS is not offered as a sandbox OS (Apple Silicon is only mentioned as a client build machine that must cross-compile to linux/amd64).

arm64.quote: OpenReward's sandbox infrastructure runs on `linux/amd64`. If you're building custom images on an ARM machine (e.g. Apple Silicon), you'll need to target this platform explicitly — more on this below.
arm64.note: Docs explicitly state the sandbox backend runs linux/amd64 only; custom images built on ARM machines must be cross-built for amd64, confirming no arm64 sandbox architecture is offered.

usage_api.quote: Available operations: run(), check_run(), upload(), download(), start(), stop(). Prepaid credits per organization, topped up at openreward.ai/<org>/billing.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: yes; Billing is managed at the organization level via a web dashboard; no REST API, SDK method, or CLI command to query billable usage of a specific sandbox is documented. Sandbox API only exposes lifecycle and execution methods.

locations_quote: OpenReward Sandboxes are tied to an environment workspace on OpenReward which provisions compute.
